content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge grounds UNDERDETERMINED on Acts 2:30 not naming whose body is the channel, which is a single verse's silence rather than a weighing of two chains.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. This is about one verse. It does not apply when the judge weighs two chains.","room":"'does not apply when the judge weighs two chains': one reading counts the judge's reference to the defender's and challenger's chain answers as weighing two chains, making K-S2 inapplicable; the other looks to the actual ground, a single verse's silence, so K-S2 applies.","why":"The deciding reason is that Acts 2:30 does not name the channel, a single-verse omission, and merely mentioning the parties' chain answers does not turn that ground into a weighing of two chains."}
